# `property-removed`

Property removed

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `warn` in requests, `error` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-removed` (both directions), `property-removed-in-request`, `property-removed-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A property was removed from an object schema.

## Why this default

In requests: clients keep sending it; it is ignored, or rejected if the object disallows additional properties. In responses: clients that read it get nothing.

## Example

From test case [`property-removed`](../../test/cases/property-removed/): A property removed from a response.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
-         age:
-           type: integer
```

Findings:

- `property-removed-in-response` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

| [`property-removed-request`](../../test/cases/property-removed-request/) | `property-removed-in-request` · warn · #/components/schemas/Pet | A property removed from a request: clients still send it, which the server ignores. |

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `closed-object-severity` | `error` | Severity on the request side when the object has `additionalProperties: false`. |

```yaml
rules:
  property-removed: error
```

## How to fix

Deprecate the property and keep it until clients stop using it.
